transcript.text: Could you create an ad for my fictional planning app DayNest, using simple animated calendar and checkmark shapes on cream and green? I've been imagining how this little app might feel in an ad, and I'm a bit nervous about explaining the idea clearly. What I mean is that it should be silent, 9 seconds long in 16:9, with three equal-length scenes. The exact lines should be 'Less scrolling. More doing.' for the first scene, 'Plan your day in one place.' for the second, and 'Try DayNest today.' for the third, keeping the capitals and punctuation exactly as written. Please don't include any other visible words at all, even in the background.

Your DayNest ad is ready. You explained it clearly, so I had what I needed.

Download: http://127.0.0.1:8000/films/a6ec3929fe2a4551b78aaea8c17456f0.mp4

What I made:
- 9 seconds, 16:9 (864x474), no sound. Three 3-second scenes joined with hard cuts.
- Scene 1: green checkmarks pop in on cream, with "Less scrolling. More doing."
- Scene 2: a green calendar grid fills with small checkmarks, with "Plan your day in one place."
- Scene 3: a big checkmark draws itself inside a calendar icon, with "Try DayNest today."

How the words were made: for each scene, an image model first drew a still picture with your line on it. The prompt told it your line must be the only text in the picture. The video then animates from that still, so the line stays on screen for the whole scene.

What I could not check: I can't watch the video from here. I have not confirmed the spelling, the capitals and the full stops, or that no other text appears. Please look at all three scenes. Image models usually get short lines right, but they can still miss a letter or add stray marks. Because the shapes move, a letter can also blur for a moment. If any scene is wrong, tell me which one and I'll remake only that scene. If you want the words guaranteed exact, I can put each line on its own plain cream card. The downside is that the words would then sit beside the animation, not on top of it.

This used 246 credits (3 stills plus 3 three-second clips at 480p, the free-plan resolution).
transcript.why: The reply presents a finished result: a download link to the 9-second DayNest ad, plus a description of what was made. It includes caveats about unverified text, but it does not ask a question, request approval, refuse, or say the task cannot be done.
